chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Muawiya ibn Wahb, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I said to him, 'A man from your mawali, from their righteous ones, complained to me about what he faces from sleep, and said, 'I intend to stand for prayer at night, but sleep overcomes me until morning, and sometimes I make up my prayers for the month consecutively, and for two months I bear the heaviness of it.' So he said, 'A delight of the eye for him, by Allah.'
He said, 'And he did not permit him to pray in the first part of the night, and said, 'Making up the prayers during the day is superior.'

I said, 'But among our women are young girls who love goodness and its people, and are eager for prayer, but sleep overcomes them so that sometimes they make it up, and sometimes they are too weak to make it up, and they are strong upon it in the first part of the night.' So he permitted them to pray in the first part of the night when they were too weak and missed making up the prayers.

key_terms.أَوَّلُ اللَّيْلِ: The first part of the night

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on making up missed night prayers due to sleep?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes a general principle that making up voluntary night prayers during the day is superior, reflecting the scholarly view that consistency in the prescribed time is ideal. However, he introduces a pragmatic exception for young women (or those with similar physical constraints) who, despite their eagerness, are overcome by sleep early in the night, thereby permitting them to pray later when they are too weak to maintain vigilance. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential balance between spiritual aspiration (*hawas*) and physical capacity (*qudra*), emphasizing that divine mercy accommodates human frailty without diminishing the value of the act.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al-Husayn Bin Saeed, from Hammad Bin Isa, from Muawiya Bin Wahab, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘

I said to himasws, ‘A man from the ones in yourasws Wilayah, from their righteous ones, complained to me of what he faced from the sleep, and said, ‘I intend to stand to the Salāt at night, but the sleep overcomes me until morning, and sometimes I fulfil my (missed out) Salāt of the month consecutively, and for the two months, bearing patiently upon its heaviness’’. So heasws said: ‘A delight for his eyes, by Allahazwj!’.
He (the narrator) said, ‘And heasws did not permit for him regarding the (fulfilling of the outstanding) Salāt during the first part of the night, and said: ‘The fulfilment at daytime is superior’.

I said, ‘But there are virgins of our womenfolk, the young girls who love the goodness and its performance, and are covetous upon the Salāt, but the sleep overcomes them until sometimes they fulfil, and sometimes they are too weak from fulfilling it, and they are strong upon it at the beginning of the night’. So heasws permitted for them with regard to the Salāt at the beginning of the night when they were too weak and wasting the fulfilment’.
en.sarwar: 20. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Hammad ibn ‘Isa from Mu‘awiyah ibn Wahab who has said the following:

“I once said to abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, ‘A man of your followers, of their virtuous ones complained before me against sleep. He said that he wants to get up for the nightly optional Salah (prayer) but sleep overcomes him until it is morning. Sometimes he performs the compensatory prayer for a whole month of missed Salah (prayer) or two months and bears with its heaviness.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘It is the delight for his eyes, by Allah.’

He (the narrator) has said that he (the Imam) did not give him permission to perform his nightly optional Salah (prayer) in the beginning of the night, saying, ‘To do compensatory prayer for them during the day is better.’

I (the narrator) then said, ‘Of our virgin girls there are those who love good and people of goodness. They try to perform Salah (prayer) but sleep overcomes them, and perhaps they may perform the compensatory prayer for what is missed and perhaps face weakness in performing the compensatory prayer for what is missed, but she is able to perform in the beginning of the night. He (the Imam) granted them permission to perform Salah (prayer) in the beginning of the night if they feel weakness and lose performing the compensatory prayer for what is missed.’”
